title: Array vs Linked List: When to Use Which?
excerpt: An array reads by index in O(1) but inserting in the middle is O(n). A linked list reaches the i-th element in O(n) but inserts after a known node in O(1).
author: BountyCode Team
body:
## Array

Elements live in one contiguous block. `arr[i]` is O(1) because the computer computes the address directly. Inserting in the middle requires shifting everything after it — O(n).

## Linked List

Each node points to the next. Reaching index i means walking from the head — O(n). But once you hold a node, inserting after it is just re-wiring two pointers — O(1).

## Arrays win most benchmarks

Because of CPU caching, contiguous memory is faster in practice even when the big-O looks similar.

## Practice it

Reverse a linked list and find the middle node using fast/slow pointers in the Linked Lists practice set.
code:
# Array: O(1) read, O(n) middle insert
arr = [10, 20, 30]
print(arr[1])            # 20, O(1)
arr.insert(1, 15)        # O(n) — shifts 20, 30 right

# Linked list (conceptual): O(n) read, O(1) insert after known node
# node.next = new_node
# new_node.next = old_next
